title: 202509_NFP Progression Rules
text:
Nottingham’s Foundation Programme Progression Regulations
Nottingham’s Foundation Programme is governed by progression regulations as outlined
below.
Award of Credit
The pass mark for a module is 40%.
The module specification states how the components of the module will be combined to
form a module mark and whether a particular mark must be gained in individual
components of the module in order for the module as a whole to be passed.
A student who fails to pass a module may nevertheless be awarded the credit for that
module in the circumstances set out in Regulations 10.
Completion (Regulation 10 in the Quality Manual)
A student who passes all the modules (as defined in the University’s Qualifications
Framework) will complete that stage and be awarded the total credit for that stage.
A student who fails one or more modules will still complete the foundation programme
and so be awarded the total credit, provided that they have:
(a) Passed modules worth at least 80 credits and have a weighted average of at least
40% with no module marks of less than 30%
or
(b) Passed modules worth at least 100 credits and have a weighted average of at
least 50%
OR
(c) Passed modules worth at least 90 credits, have marks of 30% or more in modules
worth at least 110 credits, and have a weighted average of at least 45%.
Completion of the foundation programme will allow students to progress into at least one
of the undergraduate programmes offered at the University of Nottingham Malaysia.
However, some undergraduate programmes require students to meet specific
requirements for progression. Please refer to the programme-specific progression rule in
the Programme Structure document on Nottingham’s Foundation Programme Moodle
page.

title: 2025_NFP Academic Misconduct Notice
text:
NOTITNGHAM’S FOUNDATION PROGRAMME OFFICE
PLAGIARISM AND USE OF OTHER PEOPLE’S WORK
It is in your interest to read  the following important notes on academic
misconduct.
When writing essays, reports, and assignments it is academic practice to refer to the work
of other people. On the other hand, trying to pass off other peoples’ work as one’s own is
a form of cheating, and is considered a serious misconduct both inside and outside the
University.
If you wish to use someone else’s work in what you are writing, make it quite clear to the
reader what is yours and what is the other person’s. Ask yourself what a reasonable reader
would think.
The University regulations state that:
Academic misconduct is any inappropriate activity or behaviour by a student
which may give that student, or another student, an unpermitted academic
advantage in a summative assessment and is unacceptable within the
University’s scholarly community.
Examples of academic misconduct include:
Plagiarism: Representing another person’s work or ideas as one’s own, for example by
copying and pasting content from other sources, failing to follow convention s in
acknowledging sources etc. This includes the unauthorised use of one student’s work by
another student and the commissioning, purchase and submission of a piece of work, in
part or whole, as the student’s own.
Collusion: Cooperation in order to gain an unpermitted advantage. This may occur where
students have consciously collaborated on a piece of work, in part or whole, and passed it
off as their own individual efforts or where one student has authorised another to use their
work, in part or whole, and to submit it as their own.
Note: Legitimate input from University tutors or approved readers or scribes is not
considered to be collusion.
Unauthorised use of AI : Using content generated by AI tools w hen use of AI is not
permitted for an assignment or, in cases where use of AI is permitted, failure to explicitly
acknowledge the use of AI through proper academic conventions  also cons titutes an
instance of aca demic misconduct. Refer to the Generative AI: Guidance for Students
training resource posted on the NFP Moodle page for proper guidance on what is acceptable
use of AI.
If any academic misconduct is detected in any activity which is examined, the occurrence
will be reported to the University Academic Offences Committee which has wide -ranging
disciplinary powers, including expulsion from the University if the case is proved.
At the University of Nottingham Mal aysia, you will be asked to submit your written work
to Turnitin a plagiarism checker when you turn in your assignment. Based on the report
generated by Turnitin, your instructor will exercise judgement call in determining whether
or not an instance of academic dishonesty is suspected in your work.
Please refer to the relevant section in  the quality manual  for more information on the
university’s policy and procedures on academic misconduct.

Absence
Request
(ARF)
A guide for Student V1.0
January 2026
This form allows all FND, UG and PGT active UNM students except PGR, Incoming mobility from UNUK and UNNC to submit an
absence request. Students can submit the form with or without a supporting statement from their Personal Tutor (Academic Guide)
If additional evidence or explanation is required, the Personal Tutor can use the Return to Student button to request more information.
The student must then resubmit the form, which will be processed again by the requestor (Personal tutor).
The form will be forwarded to either the Module Convenor or Head of School / Programme Director (FND) , depending on the selected
classification for the final outcome. Below are the available classifications and their corresponding approvers:
Classification selection FND &UG Final Approver
Less than 1 week + 1 Module Module Convenor
Less than 1 week + More than 2 modules Head of school / Programme Director (FND)
More than 1week + 1 Module Head of school / Programme Director (FND)
More than 1week + More than 2 modules Head of school / Programme Director (FND)
Classification selection PGT Final Approver
1-2 weekdays/1 weekend day + 1 module Module Convenor
3 weekdays/ >1 weekend day + 1 module Head of school

Go Live (February 2026)
*Please note that if you have two module absences with Less than 1 week period,
you are required to submit a separate application for each module.
